subChunks.title: Monorepo and Shared Config
subChunks.hookHtml: Enterprises and large products run multiple apps in a single monorepo: a customer-facing app, an admin dashboard, a marketing site, and a shared component library. All need the same design tokens. Getting this right — shared tokens, per-app overrides, one source of truth — prevents the design system from fragmenting into 3 competing token sets within 6 months.
subChunks.explanationHtml:
Grand Archmage Solomon: "In a monorepo, the design system CSS file is the constitution. All apps inherit it. An app may extend it — adding tokens for its specific domain. No app may contradict it without a governance decision. That discipline is what makes the system worth having."

Monorepo structure

packages/
  ui/               # Shared component library
    src/
      tokens.css    # The design system CSS
      components/
    package.json

apps/
  web/              # Customer-facing app
    src/
      index.css     # Imports tokens + app-specific overrides
  admin/            # Admin dashboard
    src/
      index.css
  marketing/
    src/
      index.css

The shared tokens file

/* packages/ui/src/tokens.css */
@import "tailwindcss";
@variant dark (&:where(.dark, .dark *));

@theme {
  /* Brand scale */
  --color-brand-50:  oklch(0.97 0.02 270);
  --color-brand-500: oklch(0.55 0.20 270);
  --color-brand-900: oklch(0.25 0.10 270);

  /* Semantic tokens */
  --color-primary:            var(--color-brand-500);
  --color-primary-foreground: oklch(0.99 0 0);
  --color-surface:            oklch(0.99 0 0);
  --color-foreground:         oklch(0.15 0 0);
  --color-border:             oklch(0.90 0 0);
  --color-error:              oklch(0.55 0.20 25);

  /* Dark mode overrides */
  /* (in .dark rule — see tw-sen-10) */

  /* Shared spacing */
  --spacing-18: 4.5rem;
  --spacing-88: 22rem;

  /* Typography */
  --font-display: "Cal Sans", sans-serif;
}

Per-app extension

/* apps/admin/src/index.css */
@import "tailwindcss";
@import "@my-org/ui/src/tokens.css"; /* Import shared tokens */

/* Admin-specific overrides and extensions */
@theme {
  /* Admin has a tighter density */
  --spacing-sidebar: 200px;  /* narrower than web's 240px */

  /* Admin accent is different from consumer brand */
  --color-admin-accent: oklch(0.55 0.15 160);  /* teal for admin */
}

/* Include admin app's source files */
@source "../src/**/*.{ts,tsx}";

Component CSS co-location

/* packages/ui/src/components/button.css */
@import "tailwindcss";

/* Components use tokens from the shared system */
@utility btn-primary {
  background: var(--color-primary);
  color: var(--color-primary-foreground);
  &:hover {
    background: oklch(from var(--color-primary) calc(l - 0.05) c h);
  }
}

/* Any app that imports tokens.css gets these utilities too */

Workspace package.json setup

// packages/ui/package.json
{
  "name": "@my-org/ui",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "exports": {
    "./tokens.css": "./src/tokens.css",
    "./components/*": "./src/components/*"
  },
  "peerDependencies": {
    "tailwindcss": "^4.0.0"
  }
}

// apps/web/package.json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "@my-org/ui": "workspace:*"
  }
}

The governance model

  • tokens.css is owned by design — changes require design review
  • Apps may add tokens — in their own index.css, not in tokens.css
  • Apps may not override brand primitives — changing --color-brand-500 in an app breaks the system
  • Semantic tokens are the API — components reference semantic tokens, never primitives directly

Solomon: "The monorepo is not a technical problem. It is a governance problem that happens to be solved with technical tools. Define ownership before you write the first line of CSS."

storyBeats.speaker: Grand Archmage Solomon
storyBeats.text: One tokens.css. Imported by all apps. Extended per app, never overridden. Components reference semantic tokens. Semantic tokens reference primitives. Only primitives change during a rebrand.

subChunks.guidedPracticeHtml:
Build a design system reference card that demonstrates the monorepo token architecture:

  • .mono-card: bg-white, rounded-2xl, border, border-gray-200, overflow-hidden, shadow-sm
  • .mono-header: bg-indigo-50, border-b, border-indigo-100, px-6, py-4
  • .mono-title: text-base, font-semibold, text-indigo-900
  • .mono-subtitle: text-xs, text-indigo-600, mt-0.5
  • .mono-body: p-6, space-y-3
  • .mono-token-row: flex, items-center, justify-between, text-sm
  • .mono-token-name: font-mono, text-gray-700
  • .mono-token-value: font-mono, text-xs, text-gray-500, bg-gray-100, px-2, py-0.5, rounded

subChunks.soloPracticeHtml: Design a monorepo design system reference UI from scratch. It should display: the token hierarchy (primitives → semantic → component), three app-level override panels (web, admin, marketing), and a visual diff showing how each app's accent colour differs from the base brand. No starter code.
subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Walk through the monorepo token architecture: what goes in the shared tokens.css, what goes in per-app index.css, and what governance rules prevent fragmentation. What is the difference between an app-specific token (allowed) and overriding a brand primitive (not allowed)?

questions.prompt: In a monorepo with a shared tokens.css, how does an app import the shared tokens?
options: Copy the tokens.css file into each app manually — CSS files cannot be imported across packages
Use a PostCSS plugin that merges all token files at build time
Extend tailwind.config.js with a preset pointing to the shared tokens file
questions.explanation: Tailwind v4 uses CSS @import for composition. Apps import the shared tokens file using the package's export path. This works because workspace packages use file system symlinks — @import resolves the package path correctly. Each app can then add its own @theme extensions after the import.

questions.prompt: The admin app needs a sidebar width of 200px (the shared system uses 240px). Where should --spacing-sidebar: 200px be defined?
options: In apps/admin/src/index.css inside a @theme block — app-specific extension that doesn't affect other apps
In packages/ui/src/tokens.css — all apps share the same sidebar width
In a CSS custom property on the sidebar element itself: style='--spacing-sidebar: 200px'
In a separate admin-tokens.css file that overrides the shared file
questions.answer: In apps/admin/src/index.css inside a @theme block — app-specific extension that doesn't affect other apps
questions.explanation: App-specific tokens belong in the app's CSS file. Adding it to the shared tokens.css would affect all apps. Putting it on the element via inline style bypasses Tailwind's utility system. A separate override file works but adds unnecessary complexity — the app's index.css is the correct place for extensions.

questions.prompt: Six months after launch, the web app's index.css contains --color-brand-500: oklch(0.53 0.17 155) to match a new brand colour. The admin and marketing apps haven't been updated. What problem has this caused?
options: The brand colour is now different across apps — web shows teal, admin and marketing show indigo — fragmenting the design system
No problem — each app overriding brand primitives independently is the intended architecture
The web app's CSS bundle increased because the override creates duplicate colour utilities
The override only affects primitives, not semantic tokens, so components still look the same
questions.answer: The brand colour is now different across apps — web shows teal, admin and marketing show indigo — fragmenting the design system
questions.explanation: Brand primitive overrides must happen in the shared tokens.css and be rolled out to all apps simultaneously. When a single app overrides a brand primitive, users see different brand colours in different parts of the product — the exact fragmentation the shared token system was designed to prevent. This is the governance violation: only semantic tokens may be overridden per-app.
